what_it_does: Many modern AI language models use a mathematical activation function called ReLU (which simply outputs zero for negative inputs and the input itself for positive ones), and this means a large fraction of the numbers flowing through the model are zero — so those multiplications can be skipped entirely to save time and energy. The trick is predicting which outputs will be zero *before* you do the full computation, so you can skip the work upfront rather than doing it and then discarding the result. Earlier prediction methods struggled when a few unusually large or small numbers (outliers) appeared in the data, causing them to mis-predict and lose the speedup. Grasp groups the numbers in each data vector by their local value range, handles those outliers explicitly, and achieves more accurate zero-prediction without needing any retraining of the model. The result is that more computation and memory traffic can be safely skipped, speeding up AI inference.
